Remaining separate groups are genuinely separate in the booklet and are intentionally not connected: the horse with its rider (b5-b9, b12) is a free-standing figure group; the fence (b155-b157, built on page 40) is a stand-alone accessory; the loose brown brick+plate (b10, b11) is only shown beside the horse.

The images are low-resolution and several pieces look alike, so the assignment of some inventory pieces to steps (366526, 366626, 447721, 3000841, 4211001, 303426, 4161412 etc.) is approximate. Every inventory piece is used and quantities match the parts list.

Parts page IDs 9327 (white minifig legs) and 9552 (red steering wheel on plate) are truncated/non-standard. They are mapped to lego-73200 (minifig legs, white) and lego-3829 (steering wheel, colour red) respectively; the exact element IDs are uncertain.
Inventory 447721 (red plate 1x10, x4) is its own type lego-447721.
Stickers (horse emblem on the SUV doors, licence plates, hazard stripes) are not parts. They are applied to bricks/tiles that are already nodes.

Port names on most stud connections are left null because the manual does not show which individual studs mate. Rod/clip, wheel hub/holder-pin and minifig leg joins also use null ports, since the catalogue port kinds do not match the real mate (pin into hub, clip on rod, legs on hip).
Wheels: 8 hubs + 8 tyres are one repeat; copies 1-4 go on the SUV wheel holders b14-b17, copies 5-8 on the trailer holders b97-b100 (attach overrides with no port).
Trailer curved panels (4541951 x2, 4497735 x4) are shown as two side panels each with an attached curved panel (step 13), plus two roof panels (step 14); the exact split is inferred.

Instruction pages are images; piece identities were read from the parts list (page 47) and step boxes. Exact stud-level placement is not recoverable from the isometric pictures, so stud/anti-stud joins are recorded part-to-part with null ports (one plate carries many joins, so single named stud ports would be wrongly reused).

Elements 383224 (1x yellow plate 2x8, used in step 7) and 4211481 (2x light-grey long tile, used in step 7) are both printed on the booklet's parts page 47 (bottom of the left and right columns, beside the Customer Service graphic, where the page's text layer is garbled: '1x 383224' and '2x ... 11 4211481', the '11' being the circled call-out for the 6178172 rod). They are real pieces used in step 7 and are kept; the earlier warning looks like a text-extraction artefact, not a wrong id.
6266219 (the two hanger plates b68/b69) is given a bar port because the stand's axle-end clip connectors (6271540) clip onto it; clip-to-bar is the compatible pair.
The 2x4 plates shown black in steps 11 and 14 are mapped to catalogue lego-302026 (the parts list calls it 302026, 3 pieces).
Step 21 flips the model; the white frame (b60, b61, b62, b63, b70) is attached to the back of the four 4x8 base plates.
The four feet (round brick 1x1 + round plate 2x2 foot, steps 27-28) sit on the frame corners; the host pieces (b60, b61, b62, b70) are an approximation.
The two eyes (step 33) are built as one sub-assembly (half-round plate + two black eye pieces) twice and placed on the forehead; hosts approximated as b97 and b86.
Piece ids b78-b85 and b98-b103 are intentionally unused; those pieces are in the foot and eye repeats.
The stand (step 26): two 11L rods, an axle extender, two elbows, two axle-end clip connectors, which clip onto the two bar plates b68/b69 on the back frame and fold out (revolute).
